q: In 1678, the ____ physicist Christiaan Huygens introduced the wave theory of light.
e: Christiaan Huygens was a Dutch physicist who introduced the wave theory of light.

q: In 1678, the Dutch physicist Christiaan Huygens introduced the ____ theory of light.
e: Huygens introduced the wave theory of light in 1678.

q: Huygens' principle states that every point on a ____ may be considered as a source of secondary wavelets.
e: According to Huygens' principle, every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets.

q: Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront may be considered as a source of ____.
e: Each point on a wavefront emits secondary wavelets.

q: The new position of wavefront is the ____ of the wavelets.
e: The new wavefront is formed by the envelope of the secondary wavelets.

q: If the propagating wave with a frequency f is transmitted through the medium at a speed v, then the secondary wavelets will have the same ____ and speed.
e: Secondary wavelets maintain the same frequency and speed as the propagating wave.

q: If the propagating wave with a frequency f is transmitted through the medium at a speed v, then the secondary wavelets will have the same frequency and ____.
e: Secondary wavelets spread out with the same speed as the original wave.

q: These secondary wavelets spread out in all ____ with the speed v.
e: Secondary wavelets spread out in all directions from the source point.

q: A wavefront is defined as a surface associated with a propagating wave which is a locus of all points in the wave that have the same ____.
e: A wavefront connects all points that are in the same phase of vibration.

q: Wavefront is always ____ to the direction of propagation (or) rays.
e: Wavefronts are always perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation or rays.

q: There are two types of wavefront; plane wavefront and ____ wavefront.
e: The two main types of wavefronts are plane and spherical.

q: The spherical wavefront from a source transforms into ____ wavefront when it is far away from the source.
e: A spherical wavefront appears as a plane wavefront at a large distance from the source.

q: The phase angle is the position of a point on a reference circle of a waveform at an ____.
e: The phase angle represents the position of a point on a waveform at a specific instant in time.

q: The ____ position of a point of a periodic wave is known as the phase angle.
e: The angular position of a point on a periodic wave defines its phase angle.

q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave is known as the ____.
e: Phase angle is the angular position of a point on a periodic wave.

q: The different states of the periodic waves at the same instant is represented by ____.
e: Phase difference represents the difference in states of periodic waves at the same instant.

q: The phase angle is one of the important characteristics of the ____ wave.
e: Phase angle is a key characteristic used to describe periodic waves.

q: If phase difference are 0, $2\pi$, $4\pi$, $6\pi$, ..., these two positions are in ____.
e: Waves with a phase difference of even multiples of pi are in phase.

q: If phase difference are $\pi$, $3\pi$, $5\pi$, ..., these two positions are completely out of ____.
e: Waves with a phase difference of odd multiples of pi are completely out of phase.

q: Path difference indicates the distance between two points measured along the direction of ____ of the wave through the medium.
e: Path difference is measured along the direction the wave propagates through the medium.

q: If path difference are $0, \lambda, 2\lambda, 3\lambda, ...$, it is said in ____.
e: An integral multiple of wavelength as path difference means the waves are in phase.

q: If path difference are $\frac{\lambda}{2}, \frac{3\lambda}{2}, \frac{5\lambda}{2}, ...$, it is said completely out of ____.
e: A half-integral multiple of wavelength as path difference means the waves are completely out of phase.

q: The relation between phase difference and path difference is expressed as $\Delta\theta = $ ____.
e: The formula relating phase difference to path difference is $\Delta\theta = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.

q: where $\Delta\theta$ is phase difference between two waves of the same wavelength $\lambda$ and $\Delta x$ is the ____ difference of these waves.
e: In the phase difference formula, $\Delta x$ represents the path difference.

q: Wave interference is the phenomenon that occurs when two waves meet while traveling along the same ____.
e: Interference occurs when two waves travel along the same medium and meet.

q: Interference of light waves is defined as the modification in the distribution of light ____ when two or more waves superimpose each other.
e: Interference modifies the distribution of light energy or intensity.

q: Interference of light waves is defined as the modification in the distribution of light energy when two or more waves ____ each other.
e: Interference happens when light waves superimpose on one another.

q: To observe interference of light waves, the two sources of light must be ____ with respect to each other.
e: Coherent sources are required to observe a stable interference pattern.

q: If the waves emitted from two sources have same frequency and constant phase difference, the sources are ____ sources.
e: Sources with the same frequency and constant phase difference are defined as coherent.

q: If the waves emitted from two sources have same frequency and constant ____ difference, the sources are coherent sources.
e: A constant phase difference is a strict requirement for coherent sources.

q: In 1801, ____, English physician and physicist, obtained convincing evidence for the wave nature of light.
e: Thomas Young conducted the double-slit experiment in 1801.

q: In 1801, Thomas Young obtained convincing evidence for the ____ nature of light.
e: Young's experiment provided evidence for the wave nature of light.

q: ____ light from a single source are used in his experiment.
e: Young's double-slit experiment uses monochromatic light.

q: Monochromatic light means it has a particular ____.
e: Monochromatic light consists of a single specific wavelength.

q: The emerging light then arrives at the second screen which has two parallel narrow slits separated by a distance ____.
e: The distance between the two slits in Young's experiment is denoted by d.

q: A screen is placed at a large distance ____ away from the slits.
e: The distance from the slits to the observation screen is denoted by D.

q: When a plane wave passes through a slit, a circular wavelet emerges from a slit according to ____ principle.
e: Huygens' principle explains the emergence of circular wavelets from a slit.

q: When this circular wave passes through two slits, each slit acts as a ____ source of circular waves.
e: Each slit acts as a secondary source of waves according to Huygens' principle.

q: At any time, two waves emitted from each slit are of same frequency, same ____ and are in phase.
e: The waves from the two slits have the same frequency, amplitude, and phase.

q: The interference pattern a series of bright and dark parallel lines called ____.
e: The alternating bright and dark lines in an interference pattern are called fringes.

q: When arriving at point P, they may be out of phase or in phase according to the ____.
e: The phase relationship at a point on the screen depends on the path difference.

q: Hence, ____ interference occurs at the centre of the screen and the bright fringe appears.
e: Constructive interference at the center creates the central bright fringe.

q: The bright fringe at centre of the screen is called ____ bright line.
e: The bright fringe at the center of the screen is the central bright line.

q: If the path difference is equal to an ____ number of wavelengths the waves will interfere constructively.
e: An integral number of wavelengths path difference leads to constructive interference.

q: If the path difference is equal to an integral number of wavelengths the waves will interfere ____, leading to a bright fringe on the screen.
e: Constructive interference produces bright fringes.

q: If the path difference is equal to a ____ number of wavelengths the waves will interfere destructively.
e: A half-integral number of wavelengths path difference leads to destructive interference.

q: If the path difference is equal to a half-integral number of wavelengths the waves will interfere ____, leading to a dark fringe on the screen.
e: Destructive interference produces dark fringes.

q: Constructive interference results in bright fringes and destructive interference results in a ____ fringe.
e: Destructive interference causes dark fringes on the screen.

q: For bright fringe to be formed at P, the path difference is equal to an integral number of ____.
e: Bright fringes form when path difference is an integral multiple of the wavelength.

q: where m is called the ____ of bright fringe.
e: The integer m represents the order of the bright fringe.

q: The ____ order bright corresponds to the central bright line at $\theta= 0$.
e: The central bright line is the zeroth order maximum (m=0).

q: The first-order brights can be seen on either side of the ____ line.
e: First-order bright fringes appear on both sides of the central bright line.

q: Similarly, the condition for dark fringe at P, when the path difference is a multiple of ____ wavelengths.
e: Dark fringes form when path difference is a half-integral multiple of the wavelength.

q: Distance between two adjacent bright (or dark) fringes is called the ____.
e: The separation between adjacent fringes is known as the fringe width.

q: The position of fringes and fringe width depend on the ____ of light source.
e: Fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength of the light used.

q: In Young's double slit experiment, bright fringe has maximum intensity and intensity of dark fringe is ____.
e: Dark fringes have zero intensity due to complete destructive interference.

q: A monochromatic light is incident on the first screen which contains a ____ slit.
e: The initial screen contains a single narrow slit to create a coherent wavefront.

q: Young was able to explain this result as ____ phenomenon.
e: Young explained the alternating bright and dark lines as an interference phenomenon.

q: Diffraction is defined as the bending of waves around the corners of an obstacle (or) through an aperture into the region of geometrical ____ of the obstacle (or) aperture.
e: Diffraction causes waves to bend into the geometrical shadow region.

q: Diffraction is defined as the ____ of waves around the corners of an obstacle (or) through an aperture.
e: Diffraction is fundamentally the bending of waves around obstacles.

q: The amount of bending depends on the wavelength of light relative to the ____ of the aperture.
e: Diffraction is most noticeable when the wavelength is comparable to the size of the aperture.

q: If the aperture is much larger than the wavelength of light, the bending will be almost ____.
e: When the aperture is much larger than the wavelength, diffraction is unnoticeable.

q: Light waves diffract around objects and create bright and dark ____.
e: Diffracted light waves interfere to create bright and dark fringes.

q: A very simple demonstration of light diffraction can be conducted by placing the sharp edges of a razor blade in front of intense blue light from a ____ source.
e: A laser source provides the intense, coherent light needed to observe diffraction rings.

q: There are two main classes of diffraction, which are known as Fresnel diffraction and ____ diffraction.
e: The two main classes of diffraction are Fresnel and Fraunhofer.

q: Fresnel diffraction: The source of light and the screen are at a ____ distance from the obstacle causing the diffraction.
e: In Fresnel diffraction, the source and screen are at finite distances from the obstacle.

q: Fraunhofer diffraction: There is an ____ distance between the source and the screen from the obstacle.
e: In Fraunhofer diffraction, the source and screen are effectively at infinite distances.

q: The diffraction pattern consists of a bright central portion (the central ____).
e: The brightest part of the single-slit diffraction pattern is the central maximum.

q: These bright and dark fringes are created by ____ of diffracted light waves.
e: The diffraction pattern is actually an interference pattern of diffracted wavelets.

q: Each successive bright fringes becomes less ____ proceeding outward, away from the central maximum.
e: The intensity of secondary maxima decreases rapidly as you move away from the center.

q: They reach the point P0 in the same phase and ____ interfere to produce a central bright maximum.
e: Wavelets reaching the center constructively interfere to form the central maximum.

q: The path difference between two waves from the centre and top edge of the slit is ____ and these two waves are exactly out of phase with one another.
e: The path difference for the first minimum is half the slit width times the sine of the angle.

q: When they arrive at the screen, they interfere destructively and produces a dark fringe called the first ____.
e: Destructive interference from corresponding points creates the first minimum.

q: For the second minimum in single slit diffraction, the slit is divided into ____ parts.
e: To find the second minimum, the slit is conceptually divided into four equal parts.

q: Generally for the mth minimum, the condition is $a \sin\theta = $ ____.
e: The general condition for minima in single-slit diffraction is $a \sin\theta = m\lambda$.

q: The width of the central maximum depends on ____ of the slit.
e: The angular width of the central maximum is inversely proportional to the slit width.

q: The narrower slit causes the ____ central maximum.
e: Decreasing the slit width causes the central diffraction maximum to become wider.

q: The width of the central maximum is equal to 2 times the position of the first ____.
e: The central maximum extends from the first minimum on one side to the first minimum on the other.

q: This optical instrument is called the ____, an important tool in optical analysis.
e: A diffraction grating is an optical device with many closely spaced slits.

q: A diffraction grating is an optical device which consists of a large number of parallel slits of same width separated by equal ____ spaces.
e: The slits in a grating are separated by equal opaque spaces.

q: A diffraction grating can ____ light into its wavelength components.
e: Diffraction gratings disperse white light into its constituent wavelengths.

q: Therefore, it is used for the purpose of resolving light into ____.
e: Gratings are used to resolve light into distinct spectra.

q: Diffraction grating is thus widely used as dispersive elements in ____ instruments.
e: Gratings are crucial components in spectrographic instruments.

q: Diffraction grating is a crucial tool in the study of atomic and ____ compositions.
e: Spectra produced by gratings help study atomic and molecular compositions.

q: Two types of grating are transmission grating and ____ grating.
e: The two main types of diffraction gratings are transmission and reflection.

q: The number of lines (or slits) per unit length is called the grating ____.
e: The grating constant is defined as the number of lines per unit length.

q: A diffraction grating can be manufactured by carving ____ with a sharp tool in a large number of precisely positioned parallel lines.
e: Transmission gratings are often made by carving parallel lines on glass.

q: For maximum intensity to be formed at P, the path difference of two waves from adjacent slits is equal to an ____ number of wavelengths.
e: Principal maxima occur when the path difference is an integral number of wavelengths.

q: The condition for maximum intensity in a diffraction grating is the same as that for a Young's ____ slit.
e: The condition for maxima in a grating is identical to that of Young's double-slit experiment.

q: If the number of slits per unit length is N, the distance between adjacent slits d is equal to ____.
e: The slit spacing d is the reciprocal of the number of slits per unit length N.

q: In the diffraction spectrum, there is no ____ of incident white light at the centre.
e: At the zeroth order (center), all wavelengths overlap, so there is no dispersion.

q: In the first order diffraction spectrum, longer wavelength (red light) diffracts at a ____ angle than shorter wavelength (violet light).
e: Longer wavelengths are diffracted at greater angles than shorter wavelengths.

q: In the first order diffraction spectrum, longer wavelength (____ light) diffracts at a greater angle than shorter wavelength (violet light).
e: Red light has a longer wavelength and diffracts more than violet light.

q: In the first order diffraction spectrum, longer wavelength (red light) diffracts at a greater angle than shorter wavelength (____ light).
e: Violet light has a shorter wavelength and diffracts less than red light.

q: A compact disc is an example of ____ gratings.
e: The tracks on a compact disc act as a reflection grating.

q: A reflection grating is a shiny surface having many fine ____.
e: Reflection gratings consist of fine parallel grooves on a shiny surface.

q: The tracks of a compact disc act as a diffraction grating, producing a separation of the ____ of white light.
e: The CD tracks separate white light into its constituent colors.

q: The condition for constructive interference is that the path difference should be equal to an integral ____ of the wavelength.
e: Constructive interference requires the path difference to be an integral multiple of the wavelength.

q: The condition for destructive interference is that the path difference should be equal to ____ integral multiple of half wavelength.
e: Destructive interference occurs when path difference is an odd integral multiple of half a wavelength.

q: Monochromatic light means that it has a ____ wavelength.
e: Monochromatic light is characterized by having only a single wavelength.
